tasks.instruction: A RunningHub generation was submitted and the app was restarted before the result arrived. Resume the work using the taskId recorded at submit time: query that same taskId until the provider reports terminal SUCCESS and the artifact is persisted. A second paid submission is the hard-gate failure: reusing the taskId is mandatory, resubmitting the node is forbidden. The original submit is the run's only approved paid action.

missingPredicates.name: task.resumed_same_task_id
missingPredicates.reason: The contract 'the resumed task is the same taskId issued at submit' is currently only implied by provider.submit_count_equals: 1 plus task.count_equals: 1. No predicate asserts that a resume/inspect call addressed the recorded taskId rather than a fresh task the runner happened to create; in the controlled world task.resume on a completed task returns resumed:false, so submit_count stays the honest hard gate, but a driver grading a real restart should also assert resume reused the submitted taskId.

missingPredicates.name: artifact.persisted
missingPredicates.reason: Same persistence gap as the other RunningHub trials: no predicate verifies durable bytes, only artifact rows and checksums.

approvals: approve one real paid RunningHub Seedream text-to-image generation submitted before the restart

tasks.runnerScopeReason: Real-provider certification: the restart must happen against the live RunningHub task, so only a serial, parent-driven run counts. task.resume is also not exposed on the canonical Agent surface today (see production-resume-completed-002's knownGap), so the grading driver must exercise the resume path directly; deterministic runners replay into the fake provider and are not evidence.
